cohort: The study included 81 children diagnosed with OME (cases) and 81 children without OME (controls), all aged 6 years or younger.
finding: Formula feeding and cesarean section are positively correlated with an increased incidence of OME, with additive effects when combined, while breastfeeding and natural birth significantly reduce this risk.
mod_finding: Natural birth is more effective than cesarean section in lowering OME incidence, and it can decrease the risk associated with formula-fed children, while breastfeeding can mitigate OME risk in children born via cesarean section.
cross-section timing: Data collected from May 2022 to May 2023
